questions.question: When checking inside a bus, what should a driver make sure of?

options.text: Every seat can be removed easily.

questions.explanation: When checking a bus inside, make sure everything is safe and works correctly. Check that all signaling devices, like bathroom emergency buzzers, work properly.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a sign that a driver is getting tired?
questions.explanation: Signs of tiredness while driving include trouble focusing, blinking a lot, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering the last few miles, missing exits or signs, trouble holding your head up, drifting out of your lane, following too closely, hitting a shoulder rumble strip, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: If a bus breaks down while passengers are still on it, what should happen?

options.text: Another bus should push it to the destination.
The bus should be towed to its destination.
The bus should be towed to the nearest safe place so passengers can get off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bus should be towed to the nearest safe place so passengers can get off.
questions.explanation: A broken-down bus with passengers should not be towed or pushed unless absolutely necessary. If it must be moved, it should only go to the nearest safe location where passengers can safely exit.

questions.question: When a bus reaches its destination, what should the driver do?

options.text: Wait to speak until the bus stops and passengers start leaving.
Remind passengers leaving to take their belongings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remind passengers leaving to take their belongings.
questions.explanation: When arriving at a stop, remind passengers to take all their belongings before leaving the bus. It is best to make this announcement before the bus comes to a complete stop.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve while passing under the bridge.

questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under something overhead, slow down. Try to find a different route if possible.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is using high beam headlights, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your high beams to tell them to switch to low beams.
Look toward the right side of your lane until they pass.
Pull to the side of the road until they pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of your lane until they pass.
questions.explanation: If oncoming traffic is using high beams, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road until they pass. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Do not apply brakes if the vehicle is out of gear.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. If needed, also chock the wheels.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Turn off the engine right away.
Spray foam from under the vehicle.

questions.explanation: In an engine fire, turn off the engine right away. Do not open the hood if you can help it. Spray foam through the vents or from under the vehicle.

questions.question: After changing a tire, why should you stop after driving a short distance?

options.text: To check that the wheel nuts are tight.
To check that the tire has enough air pressure.
To make sure you changed the right tire.
To check that changing the tire did not damage another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check that the wheel nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop after a short distance to check that the wheel nuts are tight.

questions.question: What tread depth should front tires have in every major groove?
questions.explanation: For safe driving, front tires need a tread depth of 4/32 of an inch in every major groove. Other tires need a tread depth of 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: Baggage and freight should be stored so that:

options.text: Riders can exit through any door or window in an emergency.
It blocks an exit, as long as another exit is available.
It partially covers a door, since items can be moved quickly.
It can be removed quickly in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders can exit through any door or window in an emergency.
questions.explanation: Baggage and freight must be stored so the driver can move freely, riders can exit through any door or window in an emergency, and items cannot fall or shift and injure anyone.

questions.question: Heavy steering often means:
questions.explanation: Heavy steering usually means a front tire has failed. If your steering feels different, pull off the road safely and check your tires.

questions.question: Shaded areas of the road:

options.text: Usually have no moisture, so they cannot freeze.
Stay icy and slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay icy and slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and stay cooler longer. They can remain icy and slippery after ice has melted on other parts of the road.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.text: Required only for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip, no matter how long or short the trip is.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a warning sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include difficulty focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering recent miles driven, missing exits or signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: To avoid slowing down traffic while driving a heavy vehicle, you should:

options.text: Try to pass other vehicles while driving uphill.
Ride the brakes while driving downhill.

questions.explanation: If your heavy vehicle cannot match the speed of surrounding traffic, stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab because of:

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous because poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Traveling with a passenger to take turns driving
Scheduling trips during hours when you would normally be asleep

questions.correctAnswerText: Scheduling trips during hours when you would normally be asleep
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness, get a full night's sleep before driving, travel with someone to share driving duties, schedule trips during your normal waking hours, and avoid medications that cause drowsiness.

questions.question: Over-the-counter medication:

options.text: Is not covered by driving under the influence laws.
Can affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter and prescription medications can have side effects that affect driving ability. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances, including some over-the-counter medications.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain why you are checking each item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain why you are checking each item.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will do a complete inspection and explain what you are checking and why.
